name: Togolese Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava and plantain pounded together into a smooth, stretchy dough, is one of Togo's most essential staple starches, traditionally torn by hand to scoop up soup.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava and plantain together until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy, free of lumps.

name: Togolese Pate
description: Pâte, a smooth cornmeal porridge, is Togo's most essential everyday staple, closely related to similar porridges found throughout West Africa.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 12-15 minutes until very thick and smooth.

name: Togolese Akpan
description: Akpan, a fermented corn pudding, is a beloved Togolese breakfast, traditionally topped with sweetened yogurt or milk - real akpan ferments for a full day, so this quicker version approximates a milder version of the tang.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal with the vinegar and 1.5 cups water.
Let sit at room temperature 6-8 hours to develop a slight tang.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring often, 12-15 minutes until thick and smooth.
Chill and top with the sweetened yogurt.
